 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2025-CV-0040
 Brandon Knight, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Defendant's Original Answer
Date:
10-20-25
Counsel for defendant:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defendant denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition, and demands strict proof thereof
as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant generally denies the allegations
and requests that Plaintiff be required to prove the charges and allegations by a preponderance of the evidence.
For further answer, and without assuming any burden of proof that the law places on Plaintiff, Defendant asserts the
following affirmative defenses.
First, Plaintiff's own negligence proximately caused or contributed to the occurrence. Plaintiff failed to keep a proper
lookout, failed to confirm that the adjacent lane was clear before moving, and failed to yield the right of way as
required by Texas Transportation Code Chapter 545. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies
Code, any recovery must be reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and bars recovery if that percentage
exceeds fifty percent.
Second, the injuries and damages claimed were caused in whole or in part by the acts or omissions of persons or
entities other than Defendant, and Defendant requests submission of responsible third parties under Section 33.004.
Third, Defendant asserts its right to a credit or offset for any settlement amounts paid to Plaintiff by any other person
or entity for the same damages, and asserts that Plaintiff's recoverable medical expenses are limited to amounts
actually paid or incurred under Section 41.0105.
</page>

"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
